> Original MUI X documentation: [Simple Tree View - Expansion](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/expansion/). The examples of this page are written for R.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(muiTreeView)
library(htmltools)

# Some functions of muiMaterial, muiCharts and reactRouter, used in all the examples of this page
pkg_items <- function() {
  list(
    TreeItem(
      itemId = "muiMaterial",
      label = "muiMaterial",
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiMaterial::Button", label = "Button()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiMaterial::TextField", label = "TextField()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiMaterial::Drawer", label = "Drawer()")
    ),
    TreeItem(
      itemId = "muiCharts",
      label = "muiCharts",
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiCharts::BarChart", label = "BarChart()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiCharts::LineChart", label = "LineChart()")
    ),
    TreeItem(
      itemId = "reactRouter",
      label = "reactRouter",
      TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::RouterProvider", label = "RouterProvider()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::Route", label = "Route()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::NavLink", label = "NavLink()")
    )
  )
}
```

## Default expansion

Use `defaultExpandedItems` to expand items when the tree is created. Always give the ids in a `list()`. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/expansion/#controlled-expansion)

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(
  defaultExpandedItems = list("muiMaterial", "reactRouter"),
  pkg_items()
)
```

## Controlled expansion

Use `expandedItems` with `onExpandedItemsChange` to control the expansion from your app, for example from the Shiny server with `renderReact()`. See [controlled state in Shiny](shiny.html#controlled-state-from-the-server). [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/expansion/#controlled-expansion)

`onExpandedItemsChange` receives the ids of all the expanded items. In Shiny, use `onExpandedItemsChange = setInput("expanded", 1)` to get them in `input$expanded`. On this page, a `JS()` function writes them below the tree:

```{r}
div(
  SimpleTreeView(
    onExpandedItemsChange = JS(
      "(event, itemIds) => { document.getElementById('stv-expanded').textContent = JSON.stringify(itemIds); }"
    ),
    pkg_items()
  ),
  tags$pre("Expanded items: ", tags$span(id = "stv-expanded", "[]"))
)
```

## Track item expansion change

Use `onItemExpansionToggle` to know which item was just expanded or collapsed. It receives the event, the item id and whether the item is now expanded. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/expansion/#track-item-expansion-change)

```{r}
div(
  SimpleTreeView(
    onItemExpansionToggle = JS(
      "(event, itemId, isExpanded) => {
        document.getElementById('stv-toggle').textContent =
          itemId + (isExpanded ? ' was expanded' : ' was collapsed');
      }"
    ),
    pkg_items()
  ),
  tags$pre(tags$span(id = "stv-toggle", "No item expansion recorded"))
)
```

## Limit expansion to icon container

By default, clicking anywhere on an item expands it. Use `expansionTrigger = "iconContainer"` to expand it only when clicking on the arrow icon, so that a click on the label only selects the item. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/expansion/#limit-expansion-to-icon-container)

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(
  expansionTrigger = "iconContainer",
  pkg_items()
)
```

## Imperative API

The MUI imperative API (`apiRef`, to expand an item or check whether it is expanded from JavaScript) relies on a React hook, which is not available from R. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/expansion/#imperative-api)
